routes.description: Establish that a revisable naturalist epistemology integrates scientific knowledge without requiring a supernatural layer, accounts for the named scientific domains within a rule-governed physical picture, and supports humanly grounded morality and meaning.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if naturalism supplies coherent treatments of cosmology, fine-tuning, quantum mechanics, consciousness, agency, morality, and meaning while showing that theistic additions are unnecessary or generate expectations not borne out by the world.

motionBridge.description: Connect scientific explanations and human normative practices into a coherent naturalist worldview that addresses every principal domain named in the motion.

centralBridges.description: Show that fallible, empirically checked inquiry warrants a unified natural order without claiming that every scientific or philosophical question is settled.
Explain why self-contained cosmology and naturalistic selection mechanisms can address cosmic origins and apparent fine-tuning without design.
Show that quantum theory, emergent agency, and an unfinished neuroscience of consciousness remain compatible with physicalism.
Ground morality, plural value, and finite-life meaning in human judgments, relationships, and practices without an external moral lawgiver.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Test theism against expectations concerning revelation, suffering, religious diversity, miracles, and the observed scale and character of the universe.
Explain how naturalists may retain moral insights and community-relevant resources from religious traditions without accepting supernatural authority.

routes.description: Establish that responsible theism can integrate scientific knowledge by distinguishing established findings from metaphysical interpretation, allowing science to correct religious understandings while retaining rational commitments to divine purpose, moral order, and transcendent hope.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if scientific accounts are shown not to compel naturalism, theistic belief remains rational under responsible reexamination, and theism supplies coherent treatments of creation, persons, morality, suffering, vocation, and meaning.

motionBridge.description: Connect scientifically responsible inquiry with a theistic metaphysics that remains open to correction while addressing every principal domain named in the motion.

centralBridges.description: Distinguish empirical findings from optional metaphysical glosses and specify how established science may correct historically situated religious interpretation.
Show that complete physical mechanisms for cosmic origins and qualified fine-tuning claims remain compatible with divine creation and purpose.
Establish that quantum mechanics, physical accounts of mentality, and scientific uncertainty do not uniquely settle metaphysics, personhood, or agency.
Connect theism to a real moral order, responsible engagement with suffering, present-life vocation, and hope beyond finitude.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Explain why divine freedom, human discovery, and historically mediated revelation need not make scripture a source of detailed scientific results.
Show how inherited theistic commitments may remain rational when periodically reexamined and when apparent defeaters receive responsible consideration.

sections.title: Scientific Knowledge, Revelation, and Worldview Method
sections.rationale: This issue fixes the governing standards for integrating empirical inquiry with naturalist or theistic commitments, including revisability, rational belief maintenance, revelation, and the distinction between scientific findings and metaphysical interpretation.

sections.title: Cosmic Origins, Contingency, and Fine-Tuning
sections.rationale: Cosmology and fine-tuning provide the debate's main test of whether physical self-containment and observer selection remove an explanatory role for God or remain compatible with divine creation and purpose.

sections.title: Quantum Mechanics, Metaphysical Underdetermination, and Agency
sections.rationale: This section addresses whether quantum theory carries consequences for materialism, logic, determinism, and free will, and whether emergent agency or interpretive underdetermination best connects physics to metaphysics.

sections.title: Consciousness, Physicalism, and Personhood
sections.rationale: Consciousness and the status of persons form a direct test of physical reduction, emergent explanation, non-naturalist openness, and the limits of conclusions that may presently be drawn from neuroscience or mathematical modeling.

sections.title: Morality, Suffering, Meaning, and Human Vocation
sections.rationale: The competing accounts of moral order, humanly constructed value, evil, finite life, afterlife, plural callings, and existential meaning determine how each metaphysical picture addresses the motion beyond fundamental physics.
